problem: Learning over Subgoals Planning (LSP) predicts goodness of frontier subgoals only from local features, so it cannot exploit information seen elsewhere in the map and performs poorly (even worse than a non-learned planner) in environments where non-local cues determine the right direction.
motivation: Good long-horizon goal-directed navigation in partial maps requires remembering and relating observations from other parts of the environment (e.g. room colour seen earlier indicates which hallway leads to goal). Model-free RL approaches can use memory but are unreliable and lack completeness guarantees, so a method that uses non-local information while remaining reliable by design is desirable.
key_idea: Replace LSP's fully-connected local predictor with a graph neural network over a skeleton-based topological graph of the partial map (with a global goal node), so subgoal properties P_S, R_S, R_E are predicted from non-local information while retaining LSP's model-based reliability.
insight: Passing messages over the map graph (GATv2 layers plus a global goal node) lets the network relate observations across the map; the LSP-Local ablation, which is identical except GNN layers are replaced by per-node FC layers, does worse than even the non-learned baseline in all three environments (e.g. J-Intersection 323.46 vs 204.85 for LSP-GNN). Because the learning only feeds expected-cost planning over subgoals, wrong predictions cost performance but never prevent reaching the goal.
method: LSP planning abstraction: actions are frontier subgoals; expected cost Q = D + P_S R_S + (1-P_S)[R_E + min Q], with D from A*, and P_S, R_S, R_E learned

Graph construction: skeletonize the partial map (unknown treated as free, frontiers masked except near-centre point), keep skeleton within known space, add nodes at intersections, endpoints and subgoals, and edges from the skeleton
Global goal node: a goal node connected to every other node to propagate information across the entire map; edge feature is geodesic distance, giving each node its distance to goal
Node features: 6-D (3-way one-hot semantic class/colour, neighbour count, is-subgoal flag, is-goal flag); one edge feature (geodesic distance)
GNN architecture: 3 node-wise FC layers (dim 8), 4 GATv2Conv layers (dim 8), final FC layer outputting 3 values (P_S logit, R_S, R_E) per node
Training: weighted cross-entropy for P_S and L1 for R_S and R_E, loss masked to subgoal nodes; 50k steps, lr 1e-3 decayed x0.6 every 10k; a separate network per environment
Data generation: offline trials using the known map to label each subgoal at every step, alternating between the known-space planner and an optimistic planner for diversity

setting.backbone: Graph neural network (3 FC + 4 GATv2Conv layers, trained from scratch) inside LSP model-based planner
setting.training_data: Offline simulated navigation trials: hundreds of trials in J-Intersection; 2,000 procedurally generated maps in Parallel Hallway; 2,000 trials across 56 MIT floorplans in University Building
setting.observation: Simulated semantic planar laser scanner building a partial semantic occupancy grid map; known goal location
setting.action_space: High-level frontier subgoals (boundaries between free and unseen space), executed with A*/grid planning
setting.simulator: Custom 2D grid-based simulator (J-Intersection, Parallel Hallway, MIT floorplan-based University Building)
setting.privileged: Goal location is known (goal node in graph); ground-truth map used only to generate training labels, not at test time

numbers_note: Custom environments; only average cost is reported (no SR/SPL); success is stated to be 100% by design.
results: LSP-GNN matches the fully-known planner in J-Intersection (204.85 vs 303.03 non-learned and 323.46 LSP-Local). In Parallel Hallway it cuts cost by 31.3% vs non-learned and 40.2% vs LSP-Local. On held-out MIT floorplans it gets 40.80 m, 9.3% better than non-learned and 14.9% better than LSP-Local, while always reaching the goal.
limitations: Evaluated only in simulated 2D grid environments with a semantic laser sensor; no real robot or image input
A separate network is trained per environment, and the toy environments are built so that non-local cues exist; gap to the fully-known planner remains in the large maps (40.80 vs 31.77 m)
Requires known goal location and a semantic map, and no ablation beyond the LSP-Local swap
